sentence: This project studies how a gene for an immune molecule leads to a loss of immune tolerance in type 1 diabetes.
This project tries to find out the molecular mechanism that makes advanced prostate cancer resist therapy.
This project builds lung imaging methods that use magnetic resonance imaging with proton and xenon to see lung structure and function.
This project studies how a receptor on developing T cells in the thymus helps them tell self from non-self.
This project tries to find out the roles of a signaling pathway linked to glycogen synthase kinase 3 in Alzheimer’s disease.
This project works on a genome editing therapy for Alzheimer’s disease.
This project tests animal food or animal drug samples that may be adulterated and investigates animal foodborne illness outbreaks.
This project studies how calcium signaling controls membrane trafficking.
This project investigates how silencing of the repetitive genome helps melanoma cells escape the immune system.
This project develops automated image processing tools that predict side effects of radiotherapy for head and neck cancer.
This project provides tissue processing and imaging services to help eye and vision researchers.
This project tries to find targets on a type of neuron in the prefrontal cortex to treat opioid use disorder.
This project builds tools that combine brain imaging with genomics data and predict brain phenotypes.
This project builds a research curriculum focused on HIV and the health of mothers, newborns, children and adolescents.
This project tests whether artificial intelligence tools improve predictions of outcomes for patients with non-small cell lung cancer.
This project provides statistical and bioinformatic analysis of data for studies of malignant gliomas.
This project uses advanced biophysical techniques to study how helicases that repair DNA damage are controlled.
This project studies how Candida biofilms use extracellular vesicles to resist drugs and to build a protective matrix.
This project uses data from breast cancer survivors to study how hearing and vestibular problems affect physical function and well-being.
This project studies how retrotransposons make childhood cancer cells resist drugs and how the immune system can target them.
